title: Microsoft Purview: network DLP for server and VM traffic through Azure Firewall
summary: The briefing accurately separates the roadmap plans from the documented preview and correctly describes the prerequisites, enforcement settings and fail-open limits. Minor navigation improvements would make the controls easier to follow; no blocking factual errors were found.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to extend Purview data security to the network layer through Azure Firewall integration.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview extends data security controls to the network layer through integration with Azure Firewall

claims.claim: The planned protection covers sensitive text, files and AI interactions in supported network traffic.
claims.quote: helping organizations detect and protect sensitive data in supported network traffic, including text, files, and AI interactions.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes enforcing DLP policies on traffic from servers, virtual machines and other endpoints.
claims.quote: Organizations are able to enforce DLP policies on traffic from servers, virtual machines, and other endpoints

claims.claim: The printed Purview path reaches the Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers location in the policy wizard.
claims.quote: Select + Add cloud apps and scope the destination applications. ... Enable the Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers enforcement location. ... Select Create or customize advanced DLP rules > + Create rule
claims.fix: The route is correct but stops before the activities and actions named by the row. Extend controls[0].ui.path and its rendered counterpart to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Inline web traffic > Custom > Custom policy > + Add cloud apps > Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > + Create rule > Actions > Restrict browser and network activities', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/firewall/configure-network-dlp.

claims.claim: No documented automation call was found that configures this Purview network policy's destinations, activities and actions.
claims.quote: Searched: Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers New-DlpCompliancePolicy PowerShell Locations; DlpComplianceRule Network Restrict. Read policy Locations/EnforcementPlanes and rule-search excerpts: Network is named, but no complete configuration for this location is given.

claims.claim: The printed Azure portal path reaches the DLP profile Mode control after opening a firewall policy.
claims.quote: Open the firewall policy in the Azure portal. ... Select Settings > Security Profile Groups (preview) > Create security profile group. ... On the Basics tab ... select Data loss prevention (preview). ... On the Configure protections tab ... For Mode, select Alert only.
claims.fix: Add the navigation to the policy list: set controls[1].ui.path and its rendered counterpart to 'Network security > Firewall Manager > Azure Firewall Policies > firewall policy > Settings > Security Profile Groups (preview) > Create security profile group > Basics > Data loss prevention (preview) > Configure protections > Mode'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/firewall-manager/configure-ddos for the initial navigation alongside the existing source, and update the closing explanation that currently defends starting at the policy.

claims.claim: Automation for the preview DLP profile configuration is not documented as supported.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure Firewall DLP REST API PowerShell Terraform; Azure Firewall DLP securityProfiles API. Read ai-security-concepts and configure-network-dlp: Azure PowerShell, Azure CLI, Terraform and REST API are explicitly unsupported for this preview configuration.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls table and closing prose
claims.claim: The printed Azure portal path reaches the security profile group selection on a firewall policy application rule.
claims.quote: Select Rules > Application rules and edit the target rule. ... Select the security profile group that contains the DLP profile.
claims.fix: Add the navigation to the policy list: set controls[2].ui.path and its rendered counterpart to 'Network security > Firewall Manager > Azure Firewall Policies > firewall policy > Rules > Application rules > rule > security profile group'. claims.claim: No supported automation call is documented for attaching this preview DLP security profile group to application-rule traffic.
claims.quote: Searched: Azure Firewall DLP REST API PowerShell Terraform; Azure Firewall DLP securityProfiles API. Read ai-security-concepts and configure-network-dlp: this preview configuration is explicitly portal-only, despite general firewall automation.

claims.claim: The New-DlpCompliancePolicy reference has no example or dedicated parameter named for the Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers location.
claims.quote: Searched: Network and non-Microsoft secure browsers New-DlpCompliancePolicy PowerShell Locations; searched reference for Locations, Network, Browser, Inline and SASE. Read Locations/examples: EnforcementPlanes lists Network, but no example or dedicated parameter for this location.

controlChecks.governs: Which destinations, activities and actions the Purview network DLP policy applies
Whether the firewall's DLP profile monitors or blocks (Disabled, Alert only, Alert and deny)
